title: reduce-gpu-memory-and-workspace-arena-tuning-activation-checkpointing-scratch-buffers-and-scheduling
author: Aisha Kaur
description:
Motivation: reduce peak GPU memory and workspace allocation for common serving workloads by combining arena tuning, selective activation checkpointing, scratch-buffer reuse, and scheduler/kernel adjustments. This PR targets improvements on large-context generation workloads and high-throughput continuous batching where workspace blowups and fragmentation lead to OOMs or degraded throughput.

What changed (summary):
- Arena allocator tuning: reduced default chunk sizes, introduced configurable growth policy and a per-device 'preferred_chunk' heuristic to reduce fragmentation for typical generation patterns.
- Activation checkpointing: added selective checkpointing hooks for decoder blocks (configurable by model family) and a light-weight policy to enable checkpointing only when estimated peak memory > threshold.
- Scratch buffer reuse: consolidated temporary allocation paths used by kernels into a shared scratch pool with LRU reuse and per-stream partitioning.
- Kernel and scheduling adjustments: introduced a lightweight scheduling gate to prioritize short-latency requests in the continuous-batching pipeline, and added kernel launch parameters for fused attention kernels to reduce workspace need for medium sequence lengths.
- KV cache behavior: added an early-evict policy for long idle contexts and a prefetch hint to avoid large instant allocations during sudden burst-upscales.
- Tests & benchmarks: microbenchmarks for 8/16k context lengths and end-to-end canary for continuous batching.

Checklist:
- [x] Arena config defaults updated and documented
- [x] Selective checkpointing implemented with runtime flag
- [x] Scratch buffer pool implemented and integrated with GPU kernels
- [x] Scheduler adjustments gated behind runtime config, default safe behavior preserved
- [x] Benchmarks added and CI verified
- [x] Added migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers

Benchmarks (representative):
- 8k context, batch=1 generation (redwood/gpt-like): peak GPU memory down ~22% (avg across 3 runs)
- Continuous batching (p90 latency target): sustained throughput +12% with no increase in p99 latency
- Fragmentation tests: average free arena fragmentation reduced from ~18% to ~6% on sustained workloads

Impact and rollout: The changes are behind runtime flags and a new config section (serving.runtime.memory.arena & serving.runtime.checkpointing). Default behavior is conservative; we flip to the new defaults after one-week canary rollout. Dedicated and Private deployments will be given a feature flag and migration notes.

Related: ENG-1223 (arena fragmentation), ENG-1301 (checkpointing policy), SUP-421 (customer-reported OOM on 16k context).

Notes for reviewers: focus on allocator safety, interactions with the multi-stream scratch pool, and regression risk for low-memory GPUs. The checkpointing API is intentionally simple to avoid model-specific complexity in this change; follow-ups will add model family presets.

merge_summary: Squash-merged change set that reduces peak GPU memory and fragmentation via arena allocator tuning, adds selective activation checkpointing, introduces a global scratch buffer pool, and adds scheduling/kernels adjustments. All changes behind runtime flags for controlled rollout.
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory for large-context generation workloads (~20% typical). New runtime config options: serving.runtime.memory.arena.*, serving.runtime.checkpointing.*. Default rollout conservative; canary completed.
